checks.explanation: Biden withdrew from the 2024 race in July 2024, before the Democratic National Convention, and Kamala Harris became the party's nominee in his place.
Nikki Haley did not win the Republican nomination or the presidency; Trump defeated her in the primary and went on to win the general election.
Kamala Harris, not Gavin Newsom, became the Democratic nominee after Biden withdrew in July 2024.

X remained operational through 2024 and the election proceeded and was broadly viewed as legitimate, but there was no clean resolution of an organized effort to specifically 'shut down' X as a platform.

Tucker Carlson did continue expanding his show's international coverage with head-of-state interviews in early 2024 (including a high-profile Moscow interview with Vladimir Putin in February 2024), though not specifically framed around a Dubai trip as described.
Tucker Carlson's post-Fox media venture did adopt a subscription-plus-advertising model distributed across X and his own website, consistent with the prediction.
The OpenAI leadership saga continued to develop significantly through 2024, including a major safety-team exodus and a 2024-2025 restructuring toward a more conventional for-profit structure.
The OpenAI situation was far from over after Altman's reinstatement, with continued major developments through 2024-2025 including leadership departures and a corporate restructuring.
OpenAI's roughly $86 billion valuation held and a secondary share sale at that valuation proceeded in early 2024, with the company's valuation rising much further in subsequent funding rounds.
Sam Altman consolidated control of OpenAI within months of his November 2023 reinstatement, securing a reconstituted, more supportive board.
Sam Altman was not fired again and has retained strong de facto control of OpenAI through 2026.
Extensive subsequent reporting from major outlets did surface substantial new details about the internal dynamics behind Altman's firing and reinstatement throughout 2024.
Additional concrete details about the internal conflict behind Altman's firing did become public through investigative reporting in the following months.
Information about the OpenAI board saga did emerge through a series of leaks and reports over the following months.

No clear, direct litigation matching this specific 'AGI-declaration board duty' framing has materialized; the main OpenAI litigation that emerged (Musk v. OpenAI) centers on the nonprofit-to-for-profit conversion and mission fidelity rather than this specific board obligation.
No clear public record confirms whether Sam Altman appeared on the All-In Podcast within a few weeks specifically following this December 1, 2023 episode.
